claims.title: Visibility-phase Bell predictive-law geometry
claims.scope: the declared two-parameter coplanar Bell correlation family under a fixed finite setting schedule
assumptions: setting weights are identical under the compared states
nonclaims: does not establish generic evidence for simulation
does not establish a predictive metric for arbitrary quantum states

claims.title: Canonical CHSH visibility-phase L-infinity metric
claims.scope: canonical equal-weight CHSH settings in the declared visibility-phase family
assumptions: the state is represented by q=(v cos phi,v sin phi) in the unit disk
the four canonical CHSH setting pairs are used with equal weights
nonclaims: does not imply a parent substrate uses Euclidean, L-infinity, or classical bit geometry

claims.title: Constructive quadratic predictive packing
claims.scope: canonical CHSH visibility-phase unit disk for 0<epsilon<1/4
assumptions: epsilon-accurate predictive representation is measured in one-trial total variation
the approximate predictive-state packing theorem applies
nonclaims: the bound is for the declared bounded physical family, not the full universe
internal predictive bits are not parent-hardware bits

claims.title: Adaptive transcript refinement monotonicity
claims.scope: finite deterministic adaptive policies applied to the declared phase-drift Bell process
assumptions: the complete outcome transcript is retained
the length-T transcript is the prefix projection of the length-(T+1) transcript
nonclaims: does not prove strict information growth at every horizon
does not identify an optimal adaptive policy

claims.title: Bell schedule projection seminorm criterion
claims.scope: finite coplanar setting schedules in correlation-disk coordinates
assumptions: the declared visibility-phase Bell law holds
positive-weight setting directions are treated as vectors in R^2
nonclaims: the criterion concerns identifiability inside this two-dimensional observable family
it does not characterize arbitrary quantum tomography

claims.title: Two-parameter Fisher-rank identifiability
claims.scope: regular interior points of the declared visibility-phase Bell family
assumptions: standard Fisher information regularity conditions hold
the declared schedule and two-parameter model are correctly specified
nonclaims: local Fisher rank alone does not prove global identifiability
phase is degenerate at zero visibility

claims.title: Finite adaptive phase-process predictive packing
claims.scope: finite phase-hypothesis families, finite horizon, and one declared deterministic adaptive policy
assumptions: phase follows the declared deterministic drift law
outcomes follow the declared Bell law
renderer approximation is measured in horizon-transcript total variation
nonclaims: finite-horizon packing is not a universal many-body quantum lower bound
the example parity policy is not claimed optimal
